approach: Add an optional `[job_plan] thrash_effort` key (default xhigh), stored as a small Copy, ordered enum `EffortLevel` so `JobPlanConfig` stays `Copy`. In `planning_round` (planning.rs:140), after `agent_spec` builds the planner spec, raise `spec.effort` to the higher of the base effort and `thrash_effort` when `round > 1 || mechanical_passes > 0`. The raise never lowers the effort: with `verifier_effort = "max"` and the default `xhigh`, the re-plan stays at `max`. The override follows the pattern at producer.rs:339. The first attempt of round 1 and the critic spec are untouched. `invoke_and_record` records `spec.effort`, so tests read the recorded effort back with `Records::load`. The config tests, `athena.toml`, the design doc, a new decision, and the changelog follow. `reading.rs` needs no edit.

decisions.choice: Store `thrash_effort` as `EffortLevel`, a Copy enum with `PartialOrd, Ord` in declaration order low < medium < high < xhigh < max, serde lowercase. `as_str()` returns `EFFORT_LEVELS[self as usize]`, so there is one list of names. A helper `EffortLevel::raise_base(self, base: &str) -> String` returns the higher of `self` and the parsed `base`, or `self` if `base` does not parse.
decisions.reason: `JobPlanConfig` derives `Copy` (config.rs:210) and callers move it out of `Option` with `.expect(...)` (planning.rs:95-98). A String field would drop `Copy` and force edits at about 50 uses. Ordering makes the escalation a raise and never a replacement (finding 1). Indexing into `EFFORT_LEVELS` (config.rs:337) removes the drift risk in `as_str` (finding 3), and a test pins the serde names to the list.

rejected.option: A String field checked in `validate()` with `ConfigError::Effort`, like the `[models]` efforts
rejected.why: It removes `Copy` from `JobPlanConfig` and forces edits at many callers.

rejected.option: Plain replacement of the effort with `thrash_effort`
rejected.why: With `verifier_effort = "max"` the re-plan would run below the first call, the opposite of the request. This is finding 1.
It couples two keys and makes a config error of a harmless setting. A max-in-code raise needs no refusal.

decisions.choice: Escalate in `planning_round` after `agent_spec`: `if round > 1 || mechanical_passes > 0 { spec.effort = cfg.thrash_effort.raise_base(&spec.effort); }`.
decisions.reason: Both triggers are already in `Attempt` (planning.rs:89-93). The producer overrides effort this way (producer.rs:339). One condition covers a critic revise (round > 1) and a mechanical re-plan (mechanical_passes > 0 in round 1). `effort_for` and `agent_spec` stay shared and unchanged, so the critic is not touched.

rejected.option: Add a thrash flag to `agent_spec` or `Config::effort_for`
rejected.why: They serve every role and caller, so the flag could reach the critic.
The verifier's model may not produce, so no stronger allowed model exists (out of scope).

decisions.choice: A plan seeded from an earlier job (`resumed_from`, planning.rs:48) is not thrash: its first attempt keeps the configured effort. D178 says that escalating across jobs was considered and deferred, so a later job can widen the trigger on purpose (finding 6).
decisions.reason: The accepted reading and criterion 2 say the first attempt of round 1 is unchanged.

rejected.option: Treat any seeded revision as thrash
rejected.why: It widens the trigger beyond the accepted reading.

decisions.choice: An unknown `thrash_effort` is refused by serde at parse time as `ConfigError::Parse`, and not by `validate()` as `ConfigError::Effort`. D178 and the CHANGELOG bullet say so (finding 4). The tests assert that the error names both `thrash_effort` and `extreme`.
decisions.reason: The enum keeps `Copy`. The refusal is still a config error that names the key and the value, because toml's error quotes the source line.

rejected.option: Also map the serde error to `ConfigError::Effort`
rejected.why: It adds error plumbing for no operator gain, as the message already names the key and value.

Add unit tests for the default, an explicit value, the refusal, the list agreement, the raise, and the text of the repository `[job_plan]` table.

In `planning_round`, make the planner spec mutable and raise `spec.effort` to the higher of the base and `thrash_effort` when `round > 1 || mechanical_passes > 0`. Update the `plan_round` doc comment.
Add the helper `run_planned_efforts` and four tests: a critic revise, a mechanical re-plan, a one-pass accept, and a lower thrash setting that does not lower the effort.

Add `as_str(self) -> &'static str` returning `EFFORT_LEVELS[self as usize]`, `parse(&str) -> Option<EffortLevel>` by searching `EFFORT_LEVELS`, and `raise_base(self, base: &str) -> String`, which returns the higher of `self` and the parsed `base` as a string, or `self` if `base` does not parse. risks.risk: A planner call at xhigh costs more and may reach `planner_usd` ($3.00, athena.toml:212) or the 600 s timeout, which would stop planning and make thrash worse.
risks.mitigation: The caps and timeouts are unchanged and per call (out of scope), and the preflight reserve check still runs before each call (planning.rs:113). D178 names this as the tradeoff. Whether xhigh calls hit the cap is not measured here.

risks.risk: An unknown `thrash_effort` fails as a TOML parse error and not as `ConfigError::Effort`, which the `[models]` efforts use.
risks.mitigation: The error quotes the source line, so it names the key and the value. Tests assert both strings. D178 and the CHANGELOG bullet state the difference.

risks.risk: Another job may append a decision first, so the number D178 may be taken.
risks.mitigation: The producer reads the last heading in decisions.md in its snapshot (D177 in the base) and appends the next number.

risks.risk: Config files that set `[job_plan]` keep working, but the default xhigh applies to them without a line in the file.
risks.mitigation: This is intended by the reading. athena.toml sets the key explicitly, and an operator can set `thrash_effort = "high"` to turn escalation off, as the raise never goes below the base.

risks.risk: A comment or key placed between `[job_plan]` and `mode` in athena.toml would break the hestia text assertion (hestia.rs:3579).
risks.mitigation: Step 4 places the comment and the key after `max_rounds = 5`. The hestia tests and the `job_plan` CLI test run in the checks.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in config.rs next to `job_plan_defaults_are_off_and_bounded` (config.rs:1285). (a) A `[job_plan]` with no key parses to `thrash_effort == EffortLevel::Xhigh`, and `JobPlanConfig::default()` agrees. (b) `thrash_effort = "max"` parses to `Max`. (c) `thrash_effort = "extreme"` makes `Config::parse` return an error whose text contains both `thrash_effort` and `extreme`. A row is added to `bad_job_plan_settings_are_refused_naming_the_field` (config.rs:1326). (d) For each `EFFORT_LEVELS` name at index i, parsing `thrash_effort = "<name>"` gives a variant whose `as_str()` is that name, and whose order matches i. (e) `EffortLevel::Xhigh.raise_base("max") == "max"`, `Xhigh.raise_base("high") == "xhigh"`, `Xhigh.raise_base("xhigh") == "xhigh"`, and an unparsable base gives `xhigh`.
demonstrations.observes: The default is xhigh, an explicit value is read, an unknown value is refused with the key and the value named, the enum and `EFFORT_LEVELS` agree, and the raise never lowers the effort.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the field the default test does not compile. Without the enum an unknown value would be accepted or fail as an unknown field without naming the value. Without `Ord`, the raise test fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `Config::parse` (config.rs:623) over text built with `unplanned(REPO_CONFIG)`, which exists (config.rs:1286). The pure helper `EffortLevel::raise_base` is called directly. The plan's steps 1 and 2 add the field, the helper and the tests.

demonstrations.method: Inspection of the planning.rs diff plus the behavior tests of criteria 3 to 5. The `mut` planner spec in `planning_round` is raised only under `round > 1 || mechanical_passes > 0`. The critic spec in `critic_round` is not edited. The tests assert critic records at `high`. A fourth test, `a_thrash_effort_below_the_base_does_not_lower_the_planner_effort`, injects `thrash_effort = "low"` through the `[job_plan]` text and asserts the planner efforts are `["high","high"]`.
demonstrations.observes: The diff shows the condition at the planner spec only. The tests show first-attempt planner records at `high`, later ones at `xhigh`, a lower thrash setting leaving `high`, and critic records at `high`.
demonstrations.fails_without: With no condition the second planner record stays `high` and the criterion 3 and 4 tests fail. With the condition on every attempt the first record reads `xhigh` and the criterion 5 test fails. With a plain replacement, the `thrash_effort = "low"` test fails because the re-plan drops to `low`.

The fake driver and a scripted planner and critic queue are injected through `athena_with(..., planning_script(...))` (tests.rs:190, 1193). This exists today. The new helper `run_planned_efforts` is added in step 5.

demonstrations.method: New test `a_mechanical_replan_raises_the_planner_effort`. It uses `repo_with_planning(3)` and `planning_script(vec![bad_plan(), good_plan()], vec![accepting_critique()], ..)` through `run_planned_efforts`. `bad_plan()` (tests.rs:1135) creates README.md, which already exists, so Athena's plan rules give a major finding and a `RoundEnd::Mechanical` re-plan in round 1 with no critic call.
